name: AI in Early Phase Trials
blurb: Modelling, dose selection and adaptive design.
title: AI in Early Phase Trials
answer: Early phase studies are where AI modelling of dose, exposure and response can change decisions fastest. The FDA's planned AI enabled optimization pilot invites sponsors to propose such uses in early trials, under the same credibility expectations as other decision supporting AI.

reading.body:
Early phase trials are where AI dose and exposure modelling can change decisions fastest, and the FDA's planned AI enabled optimization pilot invites sponsors to propose exactly that.

The pattern is that the earliest, smallest studies carry the most decision leverage. Dose selection and adaptive design are choices made before large patient populations are enrolled, so a model that sharpens them redirects the whole program rather than trimming its edges. The FDA pilot is the mechanism for bringing those models forward, and the stated expectation is that they meet the same credibility bar as any other decision supporting AI.

For AI specifically, this is a governance story before it is a compute story. The constraint described here is evidentiary, not physical: sponsors are asked to raise dose models in meetings rather than at submission. Nothing in this data speaks to the buildings, power, or hardware that would run such models, and no compute figures are given.

What it does not cover: the pilot's scope, timing, or acceptance criteria beyond its existence, and no named sponsors, compounds, or outcomes. The single development entry is an FDA request for information, so the pilot is proposed rather than operating.

sections.body: Bring AI dose models to the FDA early, through meetings, rather than at submission.
